name: Files changed renders the reviewer-ordered diff on seeded data
description: Walks L03b on the seeded PR #482: from the PR list into the detail route, onto the Files changed tab, and over every region of the grouped diff. Like flow 11 this makes NO model call — and here that is the feature rather than a constraint on the test. Smart Diff is deterministic by construction: `GET /pulls/:id/smart-diff` classifies paths with regexes, reads `finding_lines` off the reviews already in the database, and quotes its per-file summary out of the stored patch. `server/test/smart-diff.it.test.ts` proves the recorded-calls half (every provider mock stays empty and the `jobs` table does not grow); what this flow adds is that the whole thing really reaches a browser. Four assertions carry more than their length. 'Core logic' appearing BEFORE 'Boilerplate' is the acceptance criterion — the server returns the groups in that order and the client re-imposes it from its own `GROUP_ORDER`, so a regression in either shows here. The quoted summary 'bucketKey, rateLimit' is the no-LLM claim made visible: those two identifiers were copied out of the `@@` header tails of `src/middleware/ratelimit.ts`'s patch by a pure function, and a model that invented them would say something more fluent. '1 finding' plus 'blocker' is the overlay working end to end across the join that is easiest to get quietly wrong — the seeded review carries `agent_id: null`, so a per-agent reduction keyed on the raw value would collapse it and this badge would simply not exist (see `latestFindingsPerAgent`). And `order=original` in the URL proves the toggle is real state a link can carry, not local component state. The badge-click steps sit BEFORE the order flip, and that placement is load-bearing. They were first appended AFTER the flip, and that version failed three consecutive CI runs at the same step while passing everywhere else it was tried: macOS dev and prod builds, a linux/amd64 container driving this exact runner and a production build (10/12 — the two failures were the known 04/05 sync flake), and a replay under a x20 CDP CPU throttle. The CI failure artifact pinned the mechanism to one candidate: `find … click` exited 0, the URL never changed, and the screenshot taken ~30s later shows the page still scrolled to the very TOP — but reaching this badge requires a real scroll (y≈1050 in a 577px viewport), so the click never scrolled at all. A click that resolves, exits 0, scrolls nothing and changes nothing is a click on a node the order-flip remount had DETACHED — Original order replaces the whole card subtree, and scrollIntoView plus click on a detached element is a silent no-op. Two app-side fixes were tried first and both stay, because each is a real fix for a real bug that just was not THIS bug: the `wait --fn` barrier below guards the URL-before-commit render race it names, and both badge buttons carry `scrollMarginTop` off the sticky header's measured height so a scrolled-to badge lands clear of it (an accessibility fix — Tab-focus parks there too; see client/specs/smart-diff.md). CI failed identically with both in place. So the click now happens in Smart order, where the subtree has been stable since the tab mounted and a stale node cannot exist, and a hittability probe stands directly in front of it — if a click is ever about to be swallowed again, the PROBE times out, naming the geometry, instead of the post-click assertion timing out and pointing at the app's routing. The order flip lives at the tail and re-runs the same settle battery the first visit uses before touching the radio: the tab re-entry is this flow's only other click-after-remount, and that depth of settling is exactly what already survives CI after the initial tab switch. src/api/users.ts is chosen over src/config.ts deliberately — its WARNING sorts SECOND in the panel and `FindingsPanel` expands only the first card by default, so 'Loop issues one query per user' being on screen proves the target was carried through the URL rather than merely that the tab switched. What this flow still cannot assert is the scroll inside the findings tab (agent-browser has no scroll-position locator); that is pinned in `FindingCard.test.tsx` ('scrolls into view when it is the finding the screen was navigated to'), along with the once-only guard that stops an accept or a refetch yanking the page back. Also not asserted: that `package-lock.json` starts COLLAPSED. The row is asserted present, but 'its patch text is absent' is a negative and this harness has only positive locators — that pin is `SmartDiffViewer.test.tsx`'s 'keeps the lock file collapsed'. Nor is the split-suggestion banner: the seeded PR is 47 changed lines against a 400-line threshold, so it correctly does not fire, and `server/test/smart-diff-split.test.ts` covers the case where it does. Precondition: a freshly-seeded DB where acme/payments-api PR #482 is the first repo — run via `npm run e2e:hermetic`. NOTE the seed changed in L03b: `SEED_PR_PATCHES` carries real unified-diff text for nine files and the PR row's totals are DERIVED from it, so the summary line reads '9 files · +47'. A database seeded before that has four patch-less rows and this flow will fail on the summary and on every code line. LOCATOR CASING: 'REVIEWER-ORDERED DIFF' is asserted in the RENDERED casing — `SectionLabel` applies `text-transform: uppercase`, so the catalogue's sentence-case 'Reviewer-ordered diff' would time out against a screen that is on and correct. The group labels are NOT uppercased (they are a plain 650-weight span), so those are asserted as written.

`wait --url` returns the instant the URL changes, which is BEFORE React has committed the reordered tree — and Original order replaces the whole subtree (three <section> group wrappers become flat cards), so every file card below is a new DOM node. The group headers exist in Smart order only, so their ABSENCE is positive proof the new render is on screen. This same remount is why no click follows this step: the detached OLD nodes it leaves behind are what a `find` on a starved runner can still resolve, which is what broke this flow's first version in CI
